categories.introduction: This domain covers culinary nuts, edible seeds, and nut- and seed-derived ingredients used worldwide in cooking — organized around how they're used in the kitchen, not botanical taxonomy, snack products, confectionery, or prepared foods.
categories.name: Nuts & Seeds
categories.seo_description: Culinary nuts and seeds across six groups: Tree Nuts, Peanuts, Edible Seeds, Seed Spices, Nut Products, and Seed Products.
categories.summary: Culinary nuts and seeds across six groups: Tree Nuts, Peanuts, Edible Seeds, Seed Spices, Nut Products, and Seed Products.

groups.introduction: Culinary tree nuts used whole, chopped, and roasted in cooking and baking, including almond, walnut, pecan, hazelnut, pistachio, cashew, and macadamia.
groups.name: Tree Nuts
groups.seo_description: Tree nuts range from buttery macadamia to tannic walnut, used whole, chopped, and roasted across baking and savory cooking, including almond, walnut ...
groups.summary: Tree nuts range from buttery macadamia to tannic walnut, used whole, chopped, and roasted across baking and savory cooking, including almond, walnut, pecan, hazelnut, pistachio, cashew, and macadamia.

groups.introduction: The culinary peanut group. Despite its botanical legume status, peanut is classified here by established culinary identity — how it's used in the kitchen, not its scientific family.
groups.name: Peanuts
groups.seo_description: Peanuts are botanically a legume but sit here for their established culinary identity as a nut — the savory, roasted base of peanut butter, satay sauces ...
groups.summary: Peanuts are botanically a legume but sit here for their established culinary identity as a nut — the savory, roasted base of peanut butter, satay sauces, and West African stews.

groups.introduction: Whole seeds used in cooking, baking, and garnish, including sesame, sunflower seed, pumpkin seed, flaxseed, and chia seed.
groups.name: Edible Seeds
groups.seo_description: Edible seeds cover everything from crisp toasted sesame to sprinklable chia and flax, used across baking, garnish, and snacking, including sesame ...
groups.summary: Edible seeds cover everything from crisp toasted sesame to sprinklable chia and flax, used across baking, garnish, and snacking, including sesame, sunflower seed, pumpkin seed, flaxseed, and chia seed.

groups.introduction: Edible seeds with a primary spice-like culinary function, kept separate from seeds classified as herbs and spices, such as mustard seed.
groups.name: Seed Spices
groups.seo_description: Seed spices are edible seeds used primarily for their spice-like flavoring role rather than as a snack or baking ingredient — mustard seed and similar ...
groups.summary: Seed spices are edible seeds used primarily for their spice-like flavoring role rather than as a snack or baking ingredient — mustard seed and similar herb-and-spice seeds are grouped separately.

groups.introduction: Processed nut forms with independent culinary identity, including nut flours, nut butters, and nut meals.
groups.name: Nut Products
groups.seo_description: Nut products are processed forms with their own culinary identity distinct from the whole nuts they're made from, including nut flours, nut butters, and ...
groups.summary: Nut products are processed forms with their own culinary identity distinct from the whole nuts they're made from, including nut flours, nut butters, and nut meals.

groups.introduction: Processed seed forms with independent culinary identity, including tahini and other seed pastes and flours.
groups.name: Seed Products
groups.seo_description: Seed products are processed forms with their own culinary identity distinct from the whole seeds they're made from, including tahini and other seed pastes ...
groups.summary: Seed products are processed forms with their own culinary identity distinct from the whole seeds they're made from, including tahini and other seed pastes and flours.

aroma_profile.description: Reserved aroma characteristic tags — vocabulary frozen in FOOD-10A; do not populate until post-FOOD-10B curation standards.

canonical_culinary_groups.description: Immutable group names and slugs — do not rename or add peer groups in v1.

culinary_group.description: Canonical Culinary Group value on leaf entities — aligns to immutable group slugs.

flavor_profile.description: Reserved flavor characteristic tags — vocabulary frozen in FOOD-10A; do not populate until post-FOOD-10B curation standards.

texture_profile.description: Reserved texture characteristic tags — vocabulary frozen in FOOD-10A; do not populate until post-FOOD-10B curation standards.

usage_intensity.description: Intrinsic culinary prominence in dish composition — not Pairing Engine reasoning.

domain_exclusions.beverages: Plant milks and nut/seed beverages — reserved; out of domain v1
domain_exclusions.herbs_spices: FOOD-07 — mustard seed and whole spice entities
domain_exclusions.note: Entities in these domains are cross-referenced by canonical ID only — never duplicated intrinsically.
domain_exclusions.prepared_foods: Candy, trail mix, breakfast products, and snack products — not ingredient ontology

nut_seed.description: Canonical culinary nut, edible seed, or nut/seed-derived ingredient with frozen intrinsic metadata.

nut_seed_category.description: Top-level nut & seed domain hub (single category in v1).

nut_seed_group.description: Canonical Culinary Group (Tree Nuts, Edible Seeds, Nut Products, etc.).

botanical_ownership_rule.note: Suite rule — applies when botanical lineage diverges from culinary identity; complements NUT-001.

culinary_classification_rule.description: Group assignment follows established culinary identity, not botanical taxonomy alone.

culinary_form_ownership_rule.description: Cross-domain fruit processed forms — referenced for coconut ownership; does not govern Nut & Seed entities.

functional_pairing_rule.note: Suite wine-pairing rule — referenced for completeness; FOOD-10E may introduce domain pairing rule.

processed_product_rule.description: A processed nut or seed becomes a separate canonical ingredient only when it has an independent culinary identity.

processing_ownership_rule.description: When processing creates a distinct canonical culinary ingredient versus a preparation state or alias.

schema.taxonomy_note: Groups represent culinary identity and culinary form, not botanical families. See docs/NUT_SEED_GOVERNANCE.md.
